reason: H0 never exercises the getaddrinfo service-string path changed in S1. The change introduces exact decimal parsing and validation of `service`, with behavior also conditioned on `hints->ai_flags & ARES_AI_NUMERICSERV`; existing harnesses cover DNS wire records, server CSV parsing, and optionally query-name creation, but not these inputs or outcomes.
evidence: `numeric_service_to_port` passes attacker-controlled `service` to `strtoul(service, &end, 10)` and accepts it only when `errno == 0`, `*end == '\0'`, and `val <= 65535`.
`ares_getaddrinfo_int` uses this parser both under `ARES_AI_NUMERICSERV` and after `lookup_service(service, 0)` fails, returning `ARES_ESERVICE` on rejection.
`test/ares-test-fuzz.c` feeds bytes only to `ares_dns_parse` and DNS record access/write functions.
`test/ares-test-fuzz-name.c` normally feeds its string only to `ares_set_servers_csv`; its legacy mode calls `ares_create_query` and still does not supply a service or `ares_addrinfo_hints`.

Relevant fuzz dimensions absent from H0 include empty strings, signs, whitespace, nondecimal prefixes, trailing bytes, overflow, boundary values 0 and 65535/65536, named services, and toggling `ARES_AI_NUMERICSERV`.
recommended_action: Add a harness that reaches `ares_getaddrinfo_int` through the production getaddrinfo API, fuzzing independently null-terminated `name` and `service` strings plus `ares_addrinfo_hints` values, especially `ARES_AI_NUMERICSERV`, and observing callback status and returned port data.
